task_payload.focus: Audit Click's public export layer, decorators, command core, parser, and testing harness.

task_results.notes: Proven facts: __init__.py is the public re-export layer; decorators.py builds Command/Group objects and memoizes Parameter instances; core.py concentrates Context/Command/Group/Parameter; testing.py mutates global stdio/env for isolated IO. Hypothesis: this concentration makes small parse/type edits easy to ripple into help/completion/testing.
evidence: src/click/__init__.py re-exports Command, Group, Option, Parameter plus decorator helpers, defining the public export surface.
src/click/decorators.py command()/group()/option()/argument() attach Parameter objects and turn decorated callables into Command/Group instances.
src/click/core.py make_context -> parse_args -> invoke/main is the command path; Group.invoke/resolve_command/list_commands/get_command handle subcommand dispatch.
src/click/types.py convert_type wraps arbitrary callables in FuncParamType; src/click/testing.py CliRunner.isolation/invoke patch sys streams, env, and prompt hooks for test IO isolation.

task_payload.feature: The rejectOnClear and clearQueue behavior for pending tasks.

tests_or_commands_run: python3 .../probe_m1nd.py run [ingest, search rejectOnClear, search clearQueue, search resumeNext]
sed -n on index.js, index.d.ts, index.test-d.ts, test.js, readme.md
task_results.notes: Literal m1nd search was enough here; no semantic recovery was needed.
evidence: index.js owns the runtime behavior: rejectOnClear is parsed at the top, and clearQueue either queue.clear()s or rejects queued items with AbortSignal.abort().reason.
index.d.ts documents rejectOnClear and currently types clearQueue as () => void.
test.js covers both plain clearQueue and the rejectOnClear pending-promise rejection path.
index.test-d.ts and readme.md protect the public typing/docs surface for clearQueue and rejectOnClear.

task_payload.flow: Explain what happens when setup_panic!() is installed and a release-mode panic occurs.

tests_or_commands_run: rg -n / sed -n over src/lib.rs src/panic.rs src/report.rs tests/single-panic/tests/integration.rs
task_results.notes: Release-mode proof came from the single-panic integration test; CI mode and debug-mode branches were inspected but not needed for the requested flow.
evidence: src/lib.rs setup_panic!() expands to setup_panic(|| metadata!()) (or a caller-supplied metadata expression).
src/panic.rs setup_panic installs panic::set_hook only in Human mode, builds Report::with_panic, persists it locally unless CI, then prints the human-facing message.
src/report.rs with_panic collects panic location/cause and persist() writes report-<uuid>.toml into the temp dir.
tests/single-panic/tests/integration.rs release snapshot proves the observable stderr output and the report file side effect in a release build.

task_payload.symptom: A callable instance used as a custom Click option type crashes during command construction with AttributeError because the object has no __name__ attribute.
must_answer: why it is not a parser/runtime invocation issue

task_results.notes: Most likely fault boundary: FuncParamType.__init__ in src/click/types.py. It is not a parser/runtime invocation issue because Parameter.__init__ calls convert_type during command construction, before CliRunner.invoke or parser.parse_args ever run.
evidence: m1nd search localized self.name = func.__name__ in src/click/types.py as the only direct callable-name assumption in the option-type path.
src/click/core.py Parameter.__init__ immediately calls types.convert_type(type, default), so the crash happens while building the Option object.
The seeded regression test fails at @click.option(..., type=UpperCase()) decoration time, not during argument parsing or callback invocation.
Next focused regression test: run the seeded callable-instance test plus the nearby FuncParamType ValueError message test.

task_payload.change_request: Plan a backwards-compatible change so clearQueue() returns the number of pending tasks it discarded or rejected, without touching already running tasks.

tests_or_commands_run: python3 .../probe_m1nd.py run [ingest, search rejectOnClear, search clearQueue]
task_results.notes: Plan: edit only clearQueue-related codepaths. Return the number of pending queue entries discarded/rejected; leave activeCount and already-running promises untouched. rejectOnClear must still reject each pending promise and return the same count.
evidence: index.js clearQueue already distinguishes plain queue.clear() from rejectOnClear-driven per-item rejection, so the return-count change belongs there.
index.d.ts and index.test-d.ts are the public type gates that would need clearQueue to change from void to number.
test.js already covers both clearQueue modes and can be extended to assert the returned count and unchanged activeCount semantics.
readme.md documents clearQueue/rejectOnClear today, so docs would need the new return value spelled out.

task_payload.claim: README/docs say Click supports lazy loading of subcommands at runtime.

tests_or_commands_run: rg -n lazy|get_command|list_commands README.md docs/index.rst docs/complex.md src/click/core.py
sed -n around Group.get_command/list_commands and docs/complex.md lazy group example
task_results.notes: Conclusion: no material drift. The public claim is true in the sense that Click supports lazy loading through Group extension points, but the default Group implementation remains eager and the lazy behavior lives in the custom pattern documented in docs/complex.md.
evidence: README.md and docs/index.rst both claim Click supports lazy loading of subcommands at runtime.
docs/complex.md shows the supported pattern explicitly: subclass Group, override list_commands/get_command, and lazy-load on get_command.
src/click/core.py default Group.get_command/list_commands only consult self.commands, so lazy loading is supported via customization rather than built-in automatic import behavior.
